The quote originates with Churchill, but I found some of its later iterations to be more impactful:

"Life imitates art. We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us. These extensions of our senses begin to interact with our senses. These media become a message. We shaped the alphabet and it shaped us. In keeping with the McLuhan postulate that “the medium is the message,” a literate culture should be more than mildly eager to know what books do to people."

– “A Schoolman’s Guide to Marshall McLuhan” by John M. Culkin [Source]
